Incumbent [[Maine Republican Party|Republican]] Governor [[Paul LePage]] won election to a second term, defeating [[Maine Democratic Party|Democratic]] nominee [[Mike Michaud]], the [[U.S. representative]] from [[Maine's 2nd congressional district]], and [[Independent politician|independent]] [[Eliot Cutler]], an attorney and second-place finisher from the [[2010 Maine gubernatorial election|2010 gubernatorial election]].{{cite web|url=https://bangordailynews.com/slideshow/gov-paul-lepage-wins-a-second-term-2/|title=Gov. Paul LePage wins a second term; Michaud concedes|work=The Bangor Daily News|access-date=November 15, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205015148/http://bangordailynews.com/slideshow/gov-paul-lepage-wins-a-second-term-2/|archive-date=December 5, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} This was one of nine Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Barack Obama]] won in the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]]. This is currently the most recent election that Maine elected a Republican governor. Primary elections were held on June 10, 2014. LePage was initially considered vulnerable in this race, due to persistent approval ratings below 50%. The consensus among ''[[The Cook Political Report]]'',{{cite web|url=http://cookpolitical.com/governor/charts/race-ratings|title=Ratings|access-date=September 6, 2013|archive-date=March 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130305115607/http://cookpolitical.com/governor/charts/race-ratings|url-status=dead}} ''[[Governing (magazine)|Governing]]''{{cite web |last=Jacobson |first=Louis |url=http://www.governing.com/blogs/politics/gov-handicapping-2013-2014-governors-races-tossups.html |title=Handicapping the 2013–2014 Governors Races: The Tossups |publisher=Governing.com |date=July 18, 2013 |access-date=July 25, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130805052422/http://www.governing.com/blogs/politics/gov-handicapping-2013-2014-governors-races-tossups.html |archive-date=August 5, 2013 |df=mdy-all }} and ''[[Stuart Rothenberg|The Rothenberg Political Report]]''{{cite web|url=http://rothenbergpoliticalreport.com/ratings/governor|title=Ratings|access-date=September 6, 2013}} was that the race was a "tossup" and ''Daily Kos Elections''{{cite web|url=http://www.dailykos.com/story/2013/10/06/1243548/-Daily-Kos-Elections-gubernatorial-race-ratings-Initial-ratings-for-2013-14?detail=hide|title=Daily Kos Elections gubernatorial race ratings: Initial ratings for 2013-14|access-date=November 22, 2013}} and ''[[Sabato's Crystal Ball]]''{{cite web|url=http://www.centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/articles/category/2014-governor/|title=Ratings|access-date=September 6, 2013|archive-date=September 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130910081704/http://www.centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/articles/category/2014-governor/|url-status=dead}} rated the race as "lean Democratic". On election day, LePage won the election in what was considered a minor upset. ==Background== After a close three-way election [[2010 Maine gubernatorial election|in 2010]], Republican [[Paul LePage]], the mayor of [[Waterville, Maine|Waterville]], was elected governor with 38% of the vote. He beat independent candidate Eliot Cutler, who won 36%, and Democrat [[Libby Mitchell]], the [[List of Presidents of the Maine Senate|president]] of the [[Maine Senate]], who won 19%. Republican gubernatorial nominees in Maine have failed to win a majority of the vote in 12 consecutive cycles over the last 50+ years – the longest such GOP streak in the nation.{{cite web |url=http://editions.lib.umn.edu/smartpolitics/2014/03/06/the-elusive-republican-majorit/ |title= The Elusive Republican Majority |work=Smart Politics |first=Eric |last=Ostermeier |date= March 6, 2014}} No governor has been popularly elected with less than 40 percent of the vote in two consecutive cycles in U.S. history.{{cite web |url=http://editions.lib.umn.edu/smartpolitics/2014/10/13/could-paul-lepage-become-the-f/ |title= Could Paul LePage Become the First 30/30 Governor in History? |work=Smart Politics |first=Eric |last=Ostermeier |date= October 13, 2014}} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * [[Paul LePage]], incumbent governor{{cite web|url=http://www.kjonline.com/politics/Jeb-Bush-supporters-turn-out-for-LePage-re-election-fundraiser.html|title=LePage: I'm running for re-election|publisher=Kennebec Journal|date=July 2, 2013|access-date=July 2, 2013|archive-date=July 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130705011200/http://www.kjonline.com/politics/Jeb-Bush-supporters-turn-out-for-LePage-re-election-fundraiser.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.kjonline.com/politics/With-signatures-LePage-launches-re-election-bid-.html|title=Expanding Medicaid would be 'sinful,' LePage says|publisher=Kennebec Journal |date=March 13, 2014 |access-date=March 14, 2014}} ===Polling=== {{hidden begin|titlestyle=background:#cff|title=Hypothetical polling|contentstyle=border:solid 1px silver; padding:8px; background:var(--background-color-base); color:var(--color-base);}} '''Who should challenge LePage in a primary?'''

Maybe.|last=Mistler|first=Steve|date=July 9, 2013|work=[[Portland Press Herald]]|access-date=July 9, 2013|archive-date=September 17, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130917011905/http://www.pressherald.com/blogs/capitolticker/214379251.html|url-status=dead}} ==General election== ===Candidates=== * Eliot Cutler (Independent), attorney, board member of [[Americans Elect]] and candidate for governor [[2010 Maine gubernatorial election|in 2010]] * [[Paul LePage]] (Republican), incumbent governor * [[Mike Michaud]] (Democratic), U.S. representative ===Campaign=== On January 17, 2014, Eliot Cutler announced that he had challenged LePage and Michaud to a series of policy debates, with at least one to be held in each of Maine's [[Counties of Maine|16 counties]], over the course of the campaign. Cutler noted that neither man had a primary challenger and as such the field is largely set, with plenty of time to debate. Both LePage and Michaud's campaigns criticized Cutler as issuing such a challenge only to jump-start his campaign and generate attention.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/01/17/politics/lepage-and-michaud-call-cutlers-debate-challenge-a-stunt/|title=LePage and Michaud call Cutler's debate challenge a stunt|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=January 17, 2014 |access-date=January 17, 2014}} Lee Schultheis said that his campaign was not about winning the election, but about encouraging honest conversation on the issues and working towards compromise, while criticizing the win-at-any-cost mentality in politics. He summarized his campaign as "I'm running for Governor, but not really". He had qualified for the ballot and as such had been invited to at least one debate.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/06/23/politics/maine-has-a-fourth-gubernatorial-candidate-running-for-the-2014-election-but-not-really/|title=LePage and Michaud call Cutler's debate challenge a stunt|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=July 23, 2014 |access-date=August 1, 2014}} However, citing the fact that two of three debates he had been invited to had been cancelled, as well as the difficulty of an independent working in the two-party system, he withdrew from the race on September 5, 2014. Cutler posted a video to his [[Facebook]] and [[Twitter]] accounts on May 5, 2014, where he responded to a voter's question about his candidacy potentially [[Vote splitting|splitting the vote]] again. He stated that his supporters, if they felt on the night before the election that he could not win, should vote for someone else.{{cite news|url=http://pollways.bangordailynews.com/2014/05/06/maine-politics/cutler-gives-supporters-permission-to-vote-for-someone-else/|title=Cutler gives supporters permission to vote for someone else|newspaper=Bangor Daily News|date=May 6, 2014|access-date=May 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140509070411/http://pollways.bangordailynews.com/2014/05/06/maine-politics/cutler-gives-supporters-permission-to-vote-for-someone-else/|archive-date=May 9, 2014|url-status=dead}} In July 2014, Cutler claimed that in May 2011 he had been approached by [[Maine Democratic Party]] Chairman Ben Grant to run as a Democrat in 2014, with assurances that the Party would "clear the field" in such a circumstance. Grant denied Cutler's claim, calling it "100 percent false", stating that while he had met with Cutler, that subject was not discussed. He added that the party had been focused solely on getting Mike Michaud or [[Chellie Pingree]] to run for governor. Cutler stated that he would be willing to sign an affidavit on the matter, as he remembered the conversation "very clearly". Attorney and Democratic activist [[Severin Beliveau]] disputed Cutler's claim that he had been offered a "cleared field", saying: "That's [Cutler's] ego. We all have egos, but his is in another world, in the ether somewhere." Cutler further claimed that in the spring of 2011 he was asked by then-[[Maine Republican Party]] Chairman Charlie Webster to join the Republican Party. Webster also repudiated Cutler's claim, saying that he only met Cutler as a courtesy, asking "why would Republicans want a candidate who doesn't share our views? That doesn't make sense."{{cite web|url=http://www.centralmaine.com/2014/07/26/cutler-says-democrats-asked-him-to-run-in-2014/|title=Cutler says Democrats asked him to run in 2014|publisher=Kennebec Journal |date=July 26, 2014 |access-date=July 27, 2014}} LePage stated on a WVOM-FM radio show on August 7 that he believes he will either win by a landslide or lose by a landslide, stating that his views are too different from his opponents' to result in a close race.{{cite web|url=http://www.wcsh6.com/story/news/local/augusta-waterville/2014/08/07/lepage-ill-either-win-or-lose-by-a-landslide/13742283/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140811234431/http://www.wcsh6.com/story/news/local/augusta-waterville/2014/08/07/lepage-ill-either-win-or-lose-by-a-landslide/13742283/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 11, 2014|title=LePage: I'll either win or lose by a 'landslide'|publisher=WCSH-6 TV|date=August 7, 2014|access-date=August 7, 2014}} On September 18, LePage told the editorial board of ''[[The Portsmouth Herald]]'' that he did not want their endorsement, saying his interest in it was "none, zero". He further stated "I'm not about politics. I'm about issues. I do not want be endorsed. I don't want to be mentioned in the same vein as Mike Michaud."{{cite web|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/20/politics/lepage-bets-gop-will-take-maine-house-in-2014/|title=LePage bets GOP will to be confirmed, as columnist [[Ethan Strimling]] noted that Cutler's weekly TV spending had decreased across October from $55,000 to $50,000, then $29,000, down to $4,000. The spot did not mention LePage, hoping instead to persuade Michaud supporters to vote for Cutler. Michaud campaign manager Matt McTighe called it "a desperate attempt to split the vote that is uniting to defeat Gov. LePage"{{cite web|url=http://www.msnbc.com/rachel-maddow-show/republican-governors-association-exploits-its-pawn-maine|title=Republican Governors Association exploits its pawn in Maine|publisher=MSNBC|author=Steve Benen |author-link=Steve Benen|date=October 28, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} and King, despite having endorsed Cutler, accused the RGA of "trying to trick people" and called their tactics "[dis]honest... they're trying to promote one candidate when they're really trying to promote someone else."{{cite news|url=http://contributors.pressherald.com/politics/capitol-ticker/angus-king-rga-ad-boosting-cutler-tries-trick-people/|title=Angus King: RGA ad boosting Cutler tries to 'trick people'|newspaper=Portland Press Herald|author=Steve Mistler|date=October 28, 2014|access-date=October 29, 2014|archive-date=October 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029160802/http://contributors.pressherald.com/politics/capitol-ticker/angus-king-rga-ad-boosting-cutler-tries-trick-people/|url-status=dead}} After Cutler announced that he would hold a press conference on October 29, it was speculated that he was doing so to withdraw from the race.{{cite web|url=http://politicalwire.com/archives/2014/10/29/will_cutler_drop_out_in_maine.html|title=Will Cutler Drop Out In Maine?|publisher=Political Wire|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=October 29, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141030004830/http://politicalwire.com/archives/2014/10/29/will_cutler_drop_out_in_maine.html|archive-date=October 30, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} Cutler did not announce his withdrawal but did say that he was a "realist" and acknowledged that any victory by him would be a "long shot". He said that his supporters should "vote their consciences", whether that be for LePage or Michaud. Cutler went on to say that he would not withdraw to "kowtow to party politics and allow a bunch of political polls to drown out the voices of thousands of Mainers who believe that standing for principles, ideals and ideas makes you an American, not a spoiler." However, his announcement was seen by many as "an acknowledgement that [his] campaign is over."{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/10/29/politics/cutler-to-make-election-announcement-at-impromptu-news-conference-wednesday-morning/|title=Cutler says victory is 'long shot,' tells supporters to vote accordingly|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}}{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/politics/articles/2014-10-29/cutler-trailing-in-maine-says-hes-hopeful-but-a-realist|title=Cutler, Trailing In Maine, Says He's 'Hopeful' But a 'Realist'|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|publisher=Bloomberg|date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}}{{cite news|url=http://www.pressherald.com/2014/10/29/cutler-to-hold-press-conference-wednesday-morning/|title=Cutler staying in race, insists Mainers should 'vote their conscience'|newspaper=Portland Press Herald |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} Cutler also encouraged Maine voters to support a proposed citizen initiative to implement [[Instant-runoff voting|ranked choice voting]]. Immediately after his press conference, a group of former Cutler supporters reiterated their backing of Michaud, saying that "the right thing now is to unite behind Mike Michaud."{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2014/oct/29/you-dont-have-to-vote-for-me-maine-gubernatorial-candidate-tells-supporters|title=You don't have to vote for me, Maine gubernatorial candidate tells supporters|newspaper=The Guardian |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} Shortly after, Angus King announced that he was switching his endorsement from Cutler to Michaud, explaining: "it is clear that the voters of Maine are not prepared to elect Eliot... The good news is that we still have a chance to elect a governor who will represent the majority of Maine people: my friend and colleague, Mike Michaud."{{cite news|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/10/29/eliot-cutler_n_6067914.html|title=Eliot Cutler Staying In Maine Governors Race But Tells Backers To 'Vote Their Conscience'|work=The Huffington Post|date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}}{{cite news|url=http://www.pressherald.com/2014/10/29/angus-king-switches-endorsement-from-cutler-to-michaud/|title=Angus King switches endorsement from Cutler to Michaud|newspaper=Portland Press Herald |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} Cutler stated that he was "obviously disappointed" by King's change.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/10/29/politics/elections/snowe-endorses-lepage-as-king-switches-gubernatorial-nod-from-cutler-to-michaud/|title=King switches gubernatorial nod from Cutler to Michaud; Snowe robocall to boost LePage|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=October 29, 2014 |access-date=October 29, 2014}} ====Debates==== The Michaud campaign stated on July 30 that Michaud would only participate in debates where LePage is present and not attend ones where Cutler is the only other participant, because: "we are running against Paul LePage, he's who we are looking to unseat". The LePage campaign has said they will schedule debates around the Governor's work schedule and priorities and declined to participate in a debate in the [[Lewiston, Maine|Lewiston]]/[[Auburn, Maine|Auburn]] area in September. Cutler criticized both men as "cowards" and said that they wanted voters to make their decision "on the basis of a cascade of negative television ads bought by outside special interests". Michaud's campaign responded that at least four debates have been scheduled so far.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/07/31/news/lewiston-auburn/lepage-michaud-arent-interested-in-many-public-debates/|title=LePage, Michaud aren't interested in many public debates|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=July 30, 2014 |access-date=July 31, 2014}} Despite Michaud's position on debates, he did appear at a forum on September 12 to discuss energy policy topics with only Cutler, after LePage abruptly withdrew from participating, citing what he called a change in the format of the event. The LePage campaign stated that they had thought each candidate would appear on stage separately, but learned the day of the event that the candidates would share a stage. LePage said: "If you set up a format, you've got to stick to that format" and his campaign said event organizers "attempted to arrange a setting to put politics ahead of public policy". They denied the withdrawal was politically motivated to force Michaud to debate Cutler.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/12/politics/elections/lepage-skips-candidates-heating-fuel-forum-in-portland/|title=LePage objects to format of Portland energy forum, drops out|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=September 12, 2014 |access-date=September 15, 2014}} Both the Michaud and Cutler campaigns stated they were aware of the format. Cutler offered to leave the stage while LePage spoke, but that did not change LePage's mind. Event organizers stated "there was no intent to place politics before policy" and that the issue distracted from their efforts to discuss energy policy.{{cite web|url=http://www.centralmaine.com/2014/09/12/gov-paul-lepage-refuses-to-appear-at-energy-forum/|title=Gov. Paul LePage refuses to appear at energy forum|publisher=Kennebec Journal |date=September 12, 2014 |access-date=September 15, 2014}} LePage told [[WMTW (TV)|WMTW]] Channel 8 on September 22 that he was considering not participating in any debates with Michaud,{{cite web|url=http://www.wmtw.com/politics/gov-lepage-says-he-may-not-attend-political-debates/28188518|title=Gov. LePage says he may not attend political debates|publisher=WMTW |date=September 22, 2014 |access-date=September 22, 2014}} though he was still willing to debate Cutler alone.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/22/politics/lepage-says-he-wont-appear-on-stage-with-michaud/?ref=comments|title=LePage casts doubt on debates, says he won't appear on stage with Michaud|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=September 22, 2014 |access-date=September 22, 2014}} He said he did not want to share a stage with Michaud due to his not having criticized a TV advertisement by a liberal PAC publicizing a press release where LePage called Social Security "welfare, pure and simple," which LePage later stated was not what he meant. LePage said that he used to respect Michaud but called the lack of criticism "sad". Michaud responded by issuing a statement saying that LePage was looking for an excuse to avoid debates and that he should instead use them "to set the record straight and explain why he said in a press release that Social Security is 'welfare' and why Maine's economy hasn't recovered as quickly as the rest of the country." Michaud went on to state that "It's not a gubernatorial debate without the Governor." Cutler issued a statement that both the other men should "stop playing games". Michaud stated the following day at a press conference that he would attend the six debates that his campaign agreed to, regardless of what LePage does. He stated that he expected LePage would attend once his "temper tantrum" was over.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/23/politics/michaud-refuses-to-apologize-for-independent-ad-criticizing-lepage-says-he-will-appear-in-all-debates/|title=Michaud refuses to denounce ad criticizing LePage, calls governor's opposition a 'temper tantrum'|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=September 23, 2014 |access-date=September 23, 2014}} LePage announced on September 28 that he would participate in five debates, saying "This decision has come after much reflection over the past week on the value in debating Congressman Michael Michaud, who has continually been dishonest with the Maine people about Governor LePage's stance on Social Security", and saying he wanted to set the record straight.{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/09/28/politics/lepage-reverses-position-will-participate-in-5-debates/|title=LePage reverses position, will participate in 5 debates|newspaper=Bangor Daily News |date=September 23, 2014 |access-date=September 28, 2014}} ===Endorsements=== {{Endorsements box | title = Paul LePage | list = '''Politicians''' * [[Rick Bennett (politician)|Rick Bennett]], [[Maine Republican Party]] chairman, former [[List of Presidents of the Maine Senate|president]] of the [[Maine Senate]], 2012 US Senate candidate{{cite web|url=http://lepage2014.com/videos/|title=Re-Elect Governor Paul LePage|access-date=November 15, 2014}} * [[Barbara Bush]], former [[First Lady of the United States]]{{cite news|url=http://bangordailynews.com/2014/10/23/politics/elections/george-h-w-bush-endorses-lepage-for-governor/ |title=George H.W.
